scenes.section_title:
* Primary learning objective: Differentiate between position \\(s(t)\\) relative to origin \\(O\\), net vector displacement \\(\Delta s = s_2 - s_1\\), and total scalar distance \\(s_T\\) along a rectilinear path.
* Essential and supporting perspectives: Essential: Time Perspective (tracking spatial coordinate progression over time), Directional Vector Perspective (sign convention \\(+s/-s\\)). Supporting: Representation Perspective (coordinate axis vs. \\(s-t\\) graph).
* Important evidence gaps: The source restricts basic kinematic relations to 1D straight-line paths; multi-dimensional position vectors are deferred to curvilinear motion.
scenes.generated_prompt:
Scene Type: Process
Learning Target: Distinguish position $s(t)$ from origin $O$, net vector displacement $\Delta s = s_2 - s_1$, and cumulative scalar path distance $s_T$ during direction reversals.
Scene Objects and Initial State: Horizontal 1D coordinate axis line marked with origin $O$ at center, negative ticks to left $(-10\text{ m to } 0)$, positive ticks to right $(0\text{ to } +10\text{ m})$. Particle $P$ (red sphere) initialized at $s = 0\text{ m}$ at $t = 0\text{ s}$. Position vector arrow $\mathbf{s}$ (cyan) anchored at origin $O$ extending to particle $P$. Displacement vector arrow $\mathbf{\Delta s}$ (purple) initialized with zero length. Digital readouts: Position $s = 0.0\text{ m}$, Displacement $\Delta s = 0.0\text{ m}$, Distance $s_T = 0.0\text{ m}$. Synchronized $s-t$ graph panel above axis.
Time Behavior: Time progression $t \in [0, 10\text{ s}]$ drives particle motion along horizontal axis. Motion path allows forward progression, stopping, and direction reversal.
Custom Perspectives: Directional Sign Perspective: Positive values $(+s)$ represent position to the right of origin $O$; negative values $(-s)$ represent position to the left. Vector arrow directions dynamically reflect algebraic sign.
Governing Rules: Position defined by function $s(t)$. Displacement calculated strictly as net vector change $\Delta s = s(t) - s(0)$. Distance calculated as cumulative path length $s_T(t) = \int_0^t |v(\tau)| d\tau$. When velocity changes sign, $s_T$ continues to increase monotonically while $\Delta s$ magnitude decreases.
Learner Investigations and Controls:
- Time Scrubber: Learner drags time slider $t$ from $0\text{ s}$ to $10\text{ s}$.
- Motion Profile Preset Selector: Preset A (Forward only: $s(t) = 2t$ for $t \in [4]$); Preset B (Forward and Reverse: $s(t) = 6t - t^2$ for $t \in [3]$).
- Investigation Action: Select Preset B and scrub time from $t=0$ to $t=3\text{ s}$ (peak position $s=+9\text{ m}$) and then onward to $t=6\text{ s}$ (returns to $s=0\text{ m}$).
- Visible Consequence: At $t=3\text{ s}$, $s = +9\text{ m}$, $\Delta s = +9\text{ m}$, $s_T = 9\text{ m}$. As $t$ advances from $3\text{ s}$ to $6\text{ s}$, particle moves left back toward origin; displacement vector arrow $\mathbf{\Delta s}$ shrinks from $+9\text{ m}$ to $0\text{ m}$, while distance counter $s_T$ increases from $9\text{ m}$ to $18\text{ m}$.
Linked Representations: Particle position on 1D axis line, endpoint of position vector arrow $\mathbf{s}$, and active data point $(t, s(t))$ on $s-t$ graph are synchronized to same spatial state.
Visual Outcome and Misconception Contrast: Demonstrates that returning to initial starting position results in zero net displacement (\\(\Delta s = 0\text{ m}\\)) despite significant physical distance traveled (\\(s_T = 18\text{ m}\\)), correcting the misconception that displacement and distance are identical scalar quantities.
Acceptance Requirements:
1. Verify $\Delta s = s(t) - s(0)$ at all times.
2. Verify $s_T$ never decreases during backward motion.
3. Verify displacement vector arrow length equals $|s(t) - s(0)|$ with direction matching sign of $(s(t) - s(0))$.
Limitations: Motion restricted strictly to 1D rectilinear paths; multi-dimensional position vectors are unsupported.

first_output.core_understanding:
* Baseline concept: A particle \\(P\\) moves along a straight line path defined by axis \\(s\\). Its location at any instant \\(t\\) is defined by position function \\(s(t)\\) measured from fixed origin \\(O\\). Displacement \\(\Delta s\\) represents net vector change in position over interval \\(\Delta t\\), while distance \\(s_T\\) accumulates total path length traveled.
* Time Perspective: Elapsed time \\(t_1 \to t_2\\). At \\(t_1\\), position is \\(s_1\\); at \\(t_2\\), position is \\(s_2\\). If the particle reverses direction during \\(\Delta t\\), displacement magnitude \\(|\Delta s|\\) becomes strictly less than total distance \\(s_T\\).
* Custom perspectives: Directional Sign Perspective: Algebraic sign (\\(+\\) or \\(-\\)) defines spatial orientation relative to origin \\(O\\).
* Perspective connections: Position function \\(s(t)\\) continuously maps time to space; direction reversals cause distance \\(s_T\\) to accumulate monotonically while displacement \\(\Delta s\\) can decrease or return to zero.
first_output.visual_first_explanation:
* Visualizing essential perspectives: A horizontal coordinate axis with origin \\(O\\), positive direction to the right \\((+s)\\), negative to the left \\((-s)\\), a moving particle dot \\(P\\) leaving a visual ghost trail, and a synchronized parallel \\(s-t\\) graph.
* Literal vs. metaphorical: The horizontal axis line and particle dot are literal physical representations; vector arrow \\(\Delta s\\) and coordinate grid lines are symbolic annotations.
* Metaphor limits: Vector arrow length visually spans coordinate difference on screen, not a solid structural link attached to the particle.
first_output.visual_scene_script:
* Normal explanatory sequence: Particle starts at origin \\(O\\) (\\(s=0\\) at \\(t=0\\)). It moves in the \\(+s\\) direction to \\(s=+5\text{ m}\\), then reverses direction to \\(s=+2\text{ m}\\).
* Alternative conditions and observable outcomes: Forward-only motion demonstrates \\(|\Delta s| = s_T\\). Reversing motion demonstrates \\(|\Delta s| < s_T\\). Returning to origin yields \\(\Delta s = 0\\) while \\(s_T > 0\\).
* Learner intervention points: Learner scrubs time slider \\(t\\), toggles direction reversal point, and compares live meters for displacement \\(\Delta s\\) versus accumulated distance \\(s_T\\).
first_output.dynamic_view_blueprint:

* Specified interactions: Drag time slider \\(t \to\\) Particle updates position \\(s(t) \to\\) Governing rule \\(\Delta s = s_2 - s_1 \text{ and } s_T = \sum |\Delta s_i| \to\\) Vector arrow adjusts length/direction while distance meter continuously accumulates.

first_output.visual_learning_outcome: * Main outcome: Learner demonstrates that displacement \\(\Delta s\\) depends strictly on initial and final positions (\\(s_2 - s_1\\)), whereas path distance \\(s_T\\) accumulates total movement regardless of direction reversals.
first_output.concept_check:
* Activity: Predict displacement \\(\Delta s\\) and total distance \\(s_T\\) for a particle moving from \\(s=0\\) to \\(s=+5\text{ m}\\) and then back to \\(s=+2\text{ m}\\).
* Expected observation: Displacement \\(\Delta s = +2\text{ m}\\); Total distance \\(s_T = 8\text{ m}\\).
* Explanation: \\(\Delta s = s_{final} - s_{initial} = 2 - 0 = +2\text{ m}\\). Total distance \\(s_T = |5 - 0| + |2 - 5| = 5 + 3 = 8\text{ m}\\).
first_output.conceptual_summary: * Rectilinear position locates a particle on a 1D coordinate axis relative to origin \\(O\\). Displacement is the directional vector net change \\(\Delta s = s_2 - s_1\\), whereas total distance \\(s_T\\) is the cumulative scalar path length.
first_output.colloquial_egyptian_explanation: * الموضع \\(s(t)\\) هو مكان الجسم على خط مستقيم بالنسبة لنقطة أصل ثابتة \\(O\\). لما الجسم يتحرك، الإزاحة \\(\Delta s\\) هي الفرق المباشر بين موقعه النهائي وموقعه الابتدائي بالاتجاه والإشارة (\\(\Delta s = s_2 - s_1\\)). أما المسافة الكلية \\(s_T\\) فدي بتجمع كل خطوة مشيها الجسم بغض النظر عن الاتجاه، حتى لو لف ورجع لنفس نقطة البداية.
first_output.laws_if_any:
* Position function: \\(s = f(t)\\)
* Displacement: \\(\Delta s = s_2 - s_1 = s(t + \Delta t) - s(t)\\)
* Total distance: \\(s_T = \sum |\Delta s_i|\\)
* Units: Meters (\\(\text{m}\\)).
first_output.real_life_example:
* لو مشيت في ممر مستقيم 10 متر للأمام وبعدين رجعت 4 متر للخلف: إزاحتك عن نقطة البداية هتبقي +6 متر، بس ساعتك الذكية هتحسب إنك مشيت مسافة إجمالية 14 متر. الخطأ الشائع بيحصل لما نخلط بين الفرق بين البداية والنهاية (الإزاحة) وبين إجمالي الطاقة والمجهود المبذول في الحركة (المسافة).

scenes.section_title:
* Primary learning objective: Differentiate between average velocity \\(v_{av} = \frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}\\) over a finite time interval and instantaneous velocity \\(v = \frac{ds}{dt}\\) at a specific moment, connecting the calculus limit \\(\lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}\\) to graphic secant and tangent slopes on an \\(s-t\\) plot.
* Essential and supporting perspectives: Essential: Time Perspective (\\(\Delta t \to 0\\) limit process), Calculus Tangent Perspective (geometric slope of \\(s-t\\) curve). Supporting: Speed vs. Velocity Vector Perspective.
* Important evidence gaps: Source focuses on single-particle 1D motion differentiation; numerical truncation errors are not covered.
scenes.generated_prompt:
Scene Type: Time Evolution
Learning Target: Differentiate average velocity $v_{av} = \Delta s / \Delta t$ from instantaneous velocity $v = ds/dt$ via time interval limit $\Delta t \to 0$ and geometric secant-to-tangent line convergence on an $s-t$ plot.
Scene Objects and Initial State: $s-t$ coordinate graph displaying cubic position curve $s(t) = 6t^2 - t^3$ for $t \in [0, 5\text{ s}]$. Fixed evaluation point $A$ highlighted on curve at $t_1 = 2.0\text{ s}, s(1) = 16.0\text{ m}$. Secondary point $B$ on curve at $t_2 = t_1 + \Delta t$. Dash-dotted secant chord (orange) passing through points $A$ and $B$. Solid tangent line (bright green) passing through point $A$ with slope $m = 12.0$. Below graph, 1D particle track showing particle $P$ at $s = 16.0\text{ m}$ with attached velocity vector arrow $\mathbf{v}$ (blue). Digital readout panel displaying $\Delta t$, $\Delta s$, $v_{av} = \Delta s / \Delta t$, and $v_{inst} = ds/dt$.
Time Behavior: Simulation allows continuous adjustment of time interval parameter $\Delta t \in [0.001\text{ s}, 2.0\text{ s}]$ and playback of physical motion time $t$.
Custom Perspectives: Slope-as-Velocity Perspective: Secant line chord slope on $s-t$ graph represents average velocity $v_{av}$; tangent line slope represents instantaneous velocity $v = ds/dt$.
Governing Rules: Average velocity $v_{av} = \frac{s(t_1 + \Delta t) - s(t_1)}{\Delta t}$. Instantaneous velocity $v(t_1) = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} v_{av} = \left.\frac{ds}{dt}\right|_{t_1} = 12t_1 - 3t_1^2$. As $\Delta t \to 0$, point $B$ approaches point $A$, secant line rotates toward tangent line, and $v_{av} \to v(t_1)$.
Learner Investigations and Controls:
- Time Interval Slider (\\(\Delta t\\)): Learner drags slider from $\Delta t = 2.0\text{ s}$ down to $\Delta t = 0.001\text{ s}$.
- Evaluation Point Slider (\\(t_1\\)): Learner shifts base evaluation point $t_1$ across $[0.5\text{ s}, 3.5\text{ s}]$.
- Investigation Action: Set $t_1 = 2.0\text{ s}$ and decrease $\Delta t$ from \\(2.0\text{ s}\\) to \\(0.001\text{ s}\\).
- Visible Consequence: At \\(\Delta t = 2.0\text{ s}\\) (\\(t_2 = 4.0\text{ s}, s_2 = 32.0\text{ m}\\)), secant line slope shows \\(v_{av} = \frac{32 - 16}{2} = 8.0\text{ m/s}\\). As slider moves to \\(\Delta t = 0.001\text{ s}\\), point \\(B\\) slides down curve to merge with \\(A\\); secant line rotates smoothly into exact alignment with green tangent line, and \\(v_{av}\\) readout updates continuously from \\(8.0 \to 10.5 \to 11.8 \to 12.0\text{ m/s}\\), matching \\(v_{inst} = 12.0\text{ m/s}\\).
Linked Representations: Tangent slope value on \\(s-t\\) graph, numerical readout \\(v_{inst}\\), and velocity vector arrow length on 1D particle track remain synchronized.
Visual Outcome and Misconception Contrast: Visually demonstrates that average velocity over a finite window does not equal instantaneous velocity at a specific moment, and proves geometrically that instantaneous velocity is the derivative slope of the position-time curve at a single point.
Acceptance Requirements:
1. Verify \\(v_{av} = 8.0\text{ m/s}\\) when \\(t_1 = 2.0\text{ s}\\) and \\(\Delta t = 2.0\text{ s}\\).
2. Verify \\(v_{av}\\) converges to \\(12.0\text{ m/s}\\) as \\(\Delta t \to 0.001\text{ s}\\).
3. Verify secant line overlays tangent line perfectly at limit \\(\Delta t \to 0\\).
Limitations: Higher-order numerical approximation errors and non-differentiable motion steps are omitted.

first_output.core_understanding:
* Baseline concept: Velocity measures time rate of change of position. Average velocity \\(v_{av}\\) divides net displacement \\(\Delta s\\) by time interval \\(\Delta t\\). Instantaneous velocity \\(v = \frac{ds}{dt}\\) is the derivative of position with respect to time at exact instant \\(t\\).
* Time Perspective: As time interval \\(\Delta t = t_2 - t_1\\) shrinks toward zero, the secant line connecting \\((t_1, s_1)\\) and \\((t_2, s_2)\\) on the \\(s-t\\) graph rotates until it becomes the tangent line at \\(t_1\\).
* Custom perspectives: Slope-as-Velocity Perspective: Tangent slope on \\(s-t\\) graph equals instantaneous velocity \\(v\\); secant slope equals \\(v_{av}\\).
* Perspective connections: Shrinking physical time interval \\(\Delta t\\) directly drives geometric secant line convergence to the tangent line, unifying calculus and physical motion.
first_output.visual_first_explanation:

* Literal vs. metaphorical: Moving particle dot and \\(s-t\\) curve are literal; secant/tangent lines and slope triangles are analytical representations.
* Metaphor limits: Visual slope angle on screen depends on graph scaling, whereas physical velocity magnitude is \\(ds/dt\\) in \\(\text{m/s}\\).
first_output.visual_scene_script:
* Normal explanatory sequence: Particle moves with position function \\(s(t) = 6t^2 - t^3\\). Learner selects \\(t_1 = 2\text{ s}\\) and adjusts \\(\Delta t\\) from \\(2\text{ s}\\) down to \\(0.001\text{ s}\\).
* Alternative conditions and observable outcomes: For large \\(\Delta t = 2\text{ s}\\) (\\(t_2 = 4\text{ s}\\)), \\(v_{av} = \frac{32 - 16}{2} = 8\text{ m/s}\\). As \\(\Delta t \to 0\\), \\(v_{av}\\) converges to exact derivative \\(v(2) = 12(2) - 3(2)^2 = 12\text{ m/s}\\).
* Learner intervention points: Adjust \\(\Delta t\\) slider, toggle tangent vs secant line overlay, observe numerical readout comparison between \\(\Delta s / \Delta t\\) and \\(ds/dt\\).
first_output.dynamic_view_blueprint:
* Map perspectives: Particle on axis, \\(s-t\\) plot, secant line overlay, tangent line overlay, digital meter comparing \\(\Delta s/\Delta t\\) to \\(ds/dt\\).
* Specified interactions: Drag \\(\Delta t\\) slider toward \\(0 \to\\) Secant endpoints merge on \\(s-t\\) curve \\(\to\\) Governing rule \\(v = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t} = \frac{ds}{dt} \to\\) Secant line snaps onto tangent line and \\(v_{av}\\) readout equals \\(v\\).

first_output.visual_learning_outcome: * Main outcome: Learner identifies instantaneous velocity as the tangent slope of the \\(s-t\\) curve and explains it as the mathematical limit of average velocity as the time interval approaches zero.
first_output.concept_check:
* Activity: For \\(s(t) = 6t^2 - t^3\\), predict whether \\(v_{av}\\) over interval \\(t \in [1, 2]\\) is greater than or less than instantaneous velocity at \\(t = 2\text{ s}\\).
* Expected observation: \\(v_{av} = 8\text{ m/s}\\), whereas \\(v(2) = 12\text{ m/s}\\).
* Explanation: Acceleration is negative (\\(a = 12 - 6t < 0\\) for \\(t > 2\\)), causing velocity to decrease across the interval, making the interval average lower than the initial instantaneous speed.
first_output.conceptual_summary: * Velocity is the rate of change of position. Average velocity \\(v_{av} = \Delta s / \Delta t\\) spans a finite time window (secant slope), whereas instantaneous velocity \\(v = ds/dt = \dot{s}\\) is the exact derivative at a single moment (tangent slope).
first_output.colloquial_egyptian_explanation: * السرعة هي معدل تغير الموضع مع الزمن. لو حسبت التغير في الموضع على فترة زمنية كبيـرة \\(\Delta t\\) بتحصل على السرعة المتوسطة \\(v_{av}\\) (ميل الخط القاطع على منحنى الموضع والزمن \\(s-t\\)). لكن لو صغرت الفترة الزمنية جداً وقربتها للصفر \\(\Delta t \to 0\\)، الخط القاطع بيبقى مماس للمنحنى وبتحسب السرعة اللحظية \\(v = ds/dt\\) في اللحظة دي بالظبط.
first_output.laws_if_any:
* Average velocity: \\(v_{av} = \frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t} = \frac{s_2 - s_1}{t_2 - t_1}\\)
* Instantaneous velocity: \\(v = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t} = \frac{ds}{dt} = \dot{s}\\)
* Speed: \\(|v| = \left|\frac{ds}{dt}\right|\\)
* Units: Meters per second (\\(\text{m/s}\\)).
first_output.real_life_example:
* لما تسافر بسيارتك من القاهرة للإسكندرية (200 كم) في ساعتين، سرعة سيارتك المتوسطة \\(v_{av}\\) بتكون 100 كم/ساعة. بس عداد السرعة في عربيتك في لحظة معينة أثناء التجاوز كان قاري 130 كم/ساعة. عداد العربية بيمثل السرعة اللحظية \\(v = ds/dt\\)، أما قسمة المسافة الكلية على الزمن الكلي بتمثل السرعة المتوسطة \\(v_{av}\\).

scenes.section_title:
* Primary learning objective: Master instantaneous acceleration \\(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d^2s}{dt^2}\\) as the derivative of velocity, and apply the time-independent differential kinematic relation \\(a\,ds = v\,dv \implies a = v \frac{dv}{ds}\\) when motion is parameterized by spatial position \\(s\\).
* Essential and supporting perspectives: Essential: Derivative Hierarchy Perspective (\\(s \to v \to a\\)), Chain Rule Differential Perspective (\\(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{dv}{ds}\frac{ds}{dt} = v\frac{dv}{ds}\\)). Supporting: Graphic Slope Perspective (\\(a\\) as slope of \\(v-t\\) curve).
* Important evidence gaps: Source restricts formulations to 1D particle kinematics without mass/force dynamic terms or rotational acceleration.
